doc.title: Epic 3 Framework Selection Decision (ADR)
doc.snippet: **DECISION: AWS Strands approved by Ricardo (2025-11-07)**. Comprehensive evaluation of 3 frameworks using MCP-assisted research. Weighted scoring: Strands 84.5% vs Simple Functions 71.5%. POC validated Mistral integration (3.4s orchestration overhead, acceptable). Key findings: Zero AWS/Bedrock dependencies confirmed, native MCP support, 47% LOC reduction (50 vs 105 lines), OpenTelemetry observability built-in. Dependency: strands-agents>=1.10.0,<2.0.0 added to pyproject.toml. Fallback: Simple Function Calling if Strands blocks implementation.

doc.title: Epic 3 Orchestration Architecture Design
doc.section: Agent Specifications + Orchestration Flow + Error Handling
doc.snippet: **3-Agent Architecture:** Retrieval Agent (wraps multi_index_search from Epic 2), Analysis Agent (LLM-powered interpretation), Synthesis Agent (answer generation + citations). **Event-Driven Coordination:** AWS Strands orchestrator coordinates sequential chain (Retrieval → Analysis → Synthesis). **State Management:** Stateless agents, context passed via tool arguments. **Error Handling:** 4-tier graceful degradation (Full → Partial Analysis → Retrieval Only → Epic 2 Fallback). **Observability:** OpenTelemetry automatic tracing + structured logging. **Performance Budget:** <12s p50 total (3s orchestration + 9s agents). **LOC Estimate:** ~350 lines total (orchestrator 50 + retrieval 80 + analysis 120 + synthesis 100). **Repository Structure:** raglite/orchestration/ module with agents/ subdirectory.

doc.title: Epic 3 Workflow Patterns
doc.section: 5 Patterns with AWS Strands Code Examples
doc.snippet: **Pattern 1: Sequential Chain (Primary)** - Retrieval → Analysis → Synthesis linear flow. Use for standard analytical queries (80% of use cases). ~12s latency. Production-ready code with @tool decorators. **Pattern 4: Error Fallback (Required)** - 4-tier graceful degradation for production reliability. Implements Tier 1 (full), Tier 2 (partial analysis), Tier 3 (retrieval only), Tier 4 (Epic 2 fallback). 99.9%+ availability target. **Pattern 2: Parallel Execution (Optimization)** - Multi-backend retrieval (vector || SQL) saves ~2-3s. Epic 3.5. **Pattern 3: Conditional Routing (Enhancement)** - Query complexity classifier routes simple queries to Epic 2 (42% latency improvement). Story 3.6. **Pattern 5: Hierarchical (Epic 4 Future)** - Master orchestrator with sub-orchestrators for multi-domain workflows.

doc.title: Epic 3 PRD - AI Intelligence & Orchestration
doc.snippet: Epic 3 implements multi-agent analytical query system using agentic orchestration. Goal: Enable multi-step reasoning and complex analytical workflows beyond Epic 2's simple retrieval. Stories 3.1-3.8 implement 3-agent architecture (Retrieval, Analysis, Synthesis) with graceful degradation. Prerequisites: Story 3.0.8 spike complete (framework selected, architecture designed). Target: <10s p50 query latency, 90%+ analytical accuracy.

doc.title: Epic 3 Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Epic 3 adds raglite/orchestration/ module (~350 LOC) using AWS Strands framework. Architecture designed in Story 3.0.8 spike. Implements Pattern 1 (Sequential Chain) and Pattern 4 (Error Fallback) as primary patterns. Integrates with Epic 2 multi-index search (raglite/retrieval/) and citation generation (raglite/retrieval/attribution). MCP tool: analytical_query_financial_documents() exposes orchestrated workflow. Dependencies: strands-agents>=1.10.0, uses existing Mistral API for orchestration.

doc.title: Story 3.0.8 - Agentic Framework Architecture Spike
doc.snippet: **Status: DONE (2025-11-07)**. Research spike to select agentic framework and design orchestration architecture. Evaluated 3 frameworks, selected AWS Strands with 84.5% weighted score. POC validated Mistral integration (no AWS/Bedrock required). Designed 3-agent architecture with 4-tier graceful degradation. Documented 5 workflow patterns. Deliverables: 3 architecture documents (~2600 lines), POC code (250 lines), framework decision approved by Ricardo. Unblocks Stories 3.1-3.8 implementation.

doc.title: Epic 2 Retrospective (Post-UAT)
doc.snippet: Epic 2 retrospective identified need for Story 3.0.8 architecture spike. Risk: Picking wrong agentic framework mid-Epic 3 → 2 weeks refactoring. Decision: Invest 3 days upfront research vs 2 weeks mid-epic rework. Led to creation of Story 3.0.8 (framework selection + architecture design). Result: Epic 3 unblocked with clear architecture and framework decision.

decision.title: Framework Selection: AWS Strands
decision.rationale: Weighted decision matrix scored AWS Strands 84.5% vs Simple Function Calling 71.5%. Key factors: 47% LOC reduction (50 vs 105 lines), native MCP integration, OpenTelemetry observability, production validation (AWS Q Developer). POC confirmed zero AWS/Bedrock dependencies. Performance overhead (3.4s) acceptable and tunable. Ricardo approved with Simple Function Calling as explicit fallback.

alternatives.alternative: Pydantic AI - Rejected (35/100 score, 240+ LOC overhead, violates minimalism)
Simple Function Calling - Fallback option (85/100 score, 105 LOC, zero dependencies)

consequences.consequence: Team learning curve: 4-6 hours for event-driven patterns
Performance overhead: 3-5s orchestration (tunable via model choice)

decision.title: Agent Architecture: 3-Agent Sequential Chain
decision.rationale: 3-agent pipeline (Retrieval → Analysis → Synthesis) provides clear separation of concerns. Retrieval reuses Epic 2 multi-index search (proven 90% accuracy). Analysis adds LLM-powered interpretation. Synthesis generates final answer with Epic 2 citation generation. Sequential chain (Pattern 1) is simplest pattern, sufficient for Epic 3 MVP. Parallel optimization deferred to Epic 3.5.

consequences.consequence: Easy testing: Each agent independently testable

decision.title: Error Handling: 4-Tier Graceful Degradation
decision.rationale: Production reliability requires graceful degradation. 4 tiers: Full orchestration (best), Partial analysis (good), Retrieval only (acceptable), Epic 2 fallback (last resort). Ensures 99.9%+ availability even if Epic 3 agents fail. Explicit degradation metadata helps users understand response quality.

consequences.consequence: User transparency: Tier metadata in responses
Monitoring: Track degradation rates per tier
